questions.question: What is the difference between rem, em, px, vh, and vw in CSS?
questions.title: rem vs em vs px vs vh vs vw — CSS Units Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between rem, em, px, vh, and vw in CSS?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** px absolute; em relative to parent font-size; rem relative to root font-size; vh/vw viewport-relative; accessibility implications of px vs rem.

**Classic weak answer:** Using px for font-size everywhere — breaks user font-size accessibility settings; rem respects them.

**Senior finish:** Introduce clamp() for fluid typography, dvh/svh/lvh (dynamic viewport units) for mobile-safe height, and prefers-color-scheme.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **rem vs em vs px vs vh vs vw — CSS Units Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the difference between rem, em, px, vh, and vw in CSS?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **px absolute; em relative to parent font-size; rem relative to root font-size; vh/vw viewport-relative; accessibility implications of px vs rem**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using px for font-size everywhere — breaks user font-size accessibility settings; rem respects them**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Introduce clamp() for fluid typography, dvh/svh/lvh (dynamic viewport units) for mobile-safe height, and prefers-color-scheme**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** px absolute; em relative to parent font-size; rem relative to root font-size; vh/vw viewport-relative; accessibility implications of px vs rem
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.content:

| **What interviewers probe** | px absolute; em relative to parent font-size; rem relative to root font-size; vh/vw viewport-relative; accessibility implications of px vs rem |
| **Weak signal (avoid)** | Using px for font-size everywhere — breaks user font-size accessibility settings; rem respects them |
| **Differentiator** | Introduce clamp() for fluid typography, dvh/svh/lvh (dynamic viewport units) for mobile-safe height, and prefers-color-scheme |
| **Proof you shipped it** | Metrics (LCP, error rate), tests, DevTools trace, or incident story |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **using px for font-size everywhere — breaks user font-size accessibility settings; rem respects them** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** px absolute; em relative to parent font-size; rem relative to root font-size; vh/vw viewport-relative; accessibility implications of px vs rem
- **Pitfall:** Using px for font-size everywhere — breaks user font-size accessibility settings; rem respects them
- **Differentiator:** Introduce clamp() for fluid typography, dvh/svh/lvh (dynamic viewport units) for mobile-safe height, and prefers-color-scheme
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **px absolute; em relative to parent font-size; rem relative to root font-size; vh/vw viewport-relative; accessibility implications of px vs rem** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Using px for font-size everywhere — breaks user font-size accessibility settings; rem respects them** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Introduce clamp() for fluid typography, dvh/svh/lvh (dynamic viewport units) for mobile-safe height, and prefers-color-scheme**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
